title: Establishing Drosophila melanogaster Crosses through the Sexing and Sorting of Pupae
author: Allison Harris

steps.title: Set up workspace and tools
steps.instruction: Arrange the stereomicroscope area with a small container of de‑ionized water (5 mL) for wetting a paintbrush, a small paintbrush, a lint‑free wipe (e.g., Kim Wipes), a micro spatula, and a silicone elastomer dish; if a silicone dish is unavailable, use a small piece of damp EVA foam.

steps.title: Prepare and label vials
steps.instruction: Prepare two new vials or bottles containing standard fly food. Label one “Strain A Females + Strain B Males” and the other “Strain A Males + Strain B Females”. Set them aside.

steps.title: Select strain A vial
steps.instruction: Choose a vial or bottle of strain A F0 flies that has pupae attached to the side. Ensure the pupae are at the brown pupal stage (P12) or later (darker appearance, visible wings and legs). Remove all adult flies from this vial.

steps.title: Extract brown pupae
steps.instruction: Using the micro spatula, place its tip next to the lateral side of a brown pupa, slide the tip between the pupa and the vial wall to release it (avoid the anterior side near the head), and gently place the freed pupa onto the silicone elastomer dish.

steps.title: Collect desired number of pupae
steps.instruction: Repeat the extraction for as many strain A brown pupae as needed, aiming for at least five pupae of each sex per vial.

steps.title: Position dish for microscopy
steps.instruction: Place the silicone elastomer dish under the stereomicroscope, center one pupa in view, and set magnification to 10–20×.

steps.title: Moisten paintbrush
steps.instruction: Dip the paintbrush tip into the 5 mL de‑ionized water, then remove excess water by gently touching the tip to a lint‑free wipe.

steps.title: Orient pupa ventral side up
steps.instruction: Using the moistened paintbrush tip, turn the pupa so its ventral side faces up, making the legs clearly visible.

steps.title: Determine sex by sex combs
steps.instruction: Inspect the first tarsal segment of the front (prothoracic) legs for sex combs; presence indicates a male, absence indicates a female. Discard any pupa whose sex cannot be confidently determined.

steps.title: Transfer pupa to labeled vial
steps.instruction: Scoop the pupa onto the paintbrush and deposit it on the side of the appropriate labeled vial from Step 2 (female → “Strain A Females + Strain B Males”; male → “Strain A Males + Strain B Females”). The damp brush helps the pupa adhere. Keep all strain A pupae together in a marked section of the vial.

steps.title: Process all strain A pupae
steps.instruction: Repeat Steps 8–10 for every brown pupa on the dish until all strain A pupae are sorted.

steps.title: Repeat for strain B
steps.instruction: Perform Steps 3–11 with strain B pupae, placing strain B males into the “Strain A Females + Strain B Males” vial and strain B females into the “Strain A Males + Strain B Females” vial, so each vial contains virgin females of one strain and virgin males of the other.

steps.title: Incubate and monitor eclosion
steps.instruction: Place the labeled vials in the appropriate environment and allow 24–48 h for most F0 pupae to eclose and begin mating. Typical survival/eclosion rates are 75–100 %; ensure at least five pupae of each sex were placed initially.

steps.title: Supplement insufficient eclosion
steps.instruction: If either strain yields too few adults, repeat the sorting process to add additional pupae to the appropriate vial; you may add pupae even when adults are present by tapping flies down, quickly removing the flug, adding the new pupa, and replacing the flug.

steps.title: Remove F0 before F1 emergence
steps.instruction: To prevent cross‑breeding, remove all adult F0 flies before the first F1 pupae appear (approximately 1 week at 25 °C).

steps.title: Reuse remaining F0 for further crosses
steps.instruction: Optionally transfer surviving adult F0 flies to a fresh vial and repeat Steps 14 and 15 while they remain alive to generate additional F1 crosses.
